title: Hagwon Sleep Debt Negotiator
oneLiner: A parent-facing tradeoff tool that compares private education spending against sleep, stress, and status pressure.
targetUser: Korean parents balancing hagwon costs, peer pressure, child fatigue, and fear of falling behind.
keyUx: Enter classes, monthly costs, commute, bedtime, and goals; the product creates a family negotiation sheet with tradeoff scenarios.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web prototype for "Hagwon Sleep Debt Negotiator". Target user: Korean parents who feel pressure to add private academies while their child loses sleep and the monthly budget keeps rising. Core UX: the user enters classes, monthly cost, commute time, bedtime, academic goal, and peer-pressure notes; the product compares status anxiety against sleep debt and outputs three family negotiation scenarios. Required sections: class cost stack, sleep debt meter, peer-pressure notes, scenario comparison, family agreement sheet, and shareable summary card. Use the calm-consumer design profile: emotionally steady guidance, warm neutral surfaces, gentle accent, clear tradeoff cards, and helper text that avoids blaming parents or children.

sourceSignals.source: Reddit r/Living_in_Korea discussion on hagwon costs
sourceSignals.evidence: Korean private education spending remains a visible status and budget pressure point for parents.
sourceSignals.action: Parents compare monthly costs, class schedules, and whether the child is falling behind.
